To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of β1‐integrin‐mediated cell‐substrate adhesion is regulated by the synergistic activation of PKC and intracellular calcium.

1) β1 integrins on granulocyticHL60 cells are activated by a combination of PKC activation and elevation of intracellular calcium; 2) β1 integrin activity is regulated by intracellular calcium; and 3) the mechanism of activation of β1integrins by PKC and calcium appears to be through synergistic effects.

1) β1 integrin expression on granulocyticHL60 cells is dependent on intracellular calcium (Ca2+); 2) the Ca2+‐dependent expression of the β1 integrin epitope is synergistic with protein kinase C (PKG) activation; and 3) the Ca2‐dependent expression of β1 integrin is required for β1 integrins to mediate cell adhesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cell adhesion to extracelluar matrix proteins by the β1 integrins.
the mechanisms by which cells attach to and move over surfaces in their environment, and how these processes are controlled by the cell.
the role of intracellular calcium in the regulation of integrin function in human leukocytes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

calcium is required for β1 integrins to become activated and bind to their extracellular matrix ligands.
